title: What Will Cost More in 2022?
rawContent:
From the supermarket to the gas pump, on-going supply chain problems and surging post-COVID demand are driving up prices in 2022.
“We’re seeing the highest inflation that we’ve seen in almost 40 years.”

The latest Food Price Index from the United Nations found global food prices are at the highest level in a decade. And experts worry continued disruptions from the pandemic like labor shortages, high costs for shipping and fertilizer could make things worse.
“Those prices have gone up quite a bit doubled, tripled some of those, some of those fertilizer prices. Farmers face a lot of difficulties getting the things that they need to produce.”

Also likely returning next year, more pain at the pump. While prices have fallen recently, a new Gasbuddy forecast predicts prices may climb to almost 4 dollars a gallon by Memorial Day.
“The economy is very strong and gasoline demand is going to be strong along with it. And that’s likely behind the push the increase in gas prices that we’re anticipating for the year ahead.”

Meanwhile, prices for electronics, clothes, and furniture could also jump next year. That’s according to a UN report that found prices for of those products could rise by more than 10 percent globally due to high shipping costs. Economists warn COVID-related production shutdowns could scramble supply chains even further.
“We’re not gonna shut down here, but China, they’ll shut down. And if China shuts down that has impacts on all those supply chains that originate in Asia.”

그리고 내년에는 석유 이용에 더 골치가 아플 것 같습니다. 최근 가격이 하락했지만, 가스버디(Gasbuddy)의 최근 전망에 따르면, 메모리얼 데이(5월 30일) 무렵에는 기름값이 갤런 당 4달러에 육박할 것이라고 합니다. “경제가 아주 좋아지면서 그에 따라 기름 수요도 많아질 것입니다. 1년을 내다봤을 때, 그것이 기름값 상승을 부추기는 배경 요인이 될 것입니다.”

한편, 전자제품, 의류, 가구 등의 가격도 내년에 오를 전망입니다. 이것은 유엔 보고서에 따른 것으로, 배송비가 더 높아짐에 따라 이 품목들의 가격이 전세계적으로 10% 이상 인상될 수 있다고 합니다. 경제학자들은 코로나와 관련된 생산 중단이 공급망에 대한 경쟁을 더 심화시킬 것이라고 경고하고 있습니다. “여기(미국)에서는 생산 중단을 하지 않을 것이지만, 중국에서는 생산을 중단할 것 같은데, 중국에서 생산을 중단하면 아시아에서 나오는 모든 공급망에 영향을 끼치게 될 것입니다.”

title: Woman’s Dad Inspires Her To Train Guide Dogs
koreanTitle: 아빠로 인해 안내견 훈련을 시작한 여성
rawContent:
“This is the current puppy that I’m raising.”

Ever since Meghan Watson was a little girl, all she’s wanted to do is raise guide dog puppies.

“I had put together a presentation of how I wanted to become a puppy raiser.”

Her passion started when her father, who is blind, received his first guide dog from Southeastern Guide Dogs in Manatee County and she saw how much it helped him.

“Whenever he was using a guide dog he can do whatever he wanted to do. He could go for a walk by himself. He could go to the grocery store.”

That passion drove Meghan to turn her dream into a reality. Now she’s on her fifth puppy-in-training for Southeastern Guide Dogs. She raises each puppy for about a year ... teaching them a foundation of guide dog skills before giving them back - something that she says is not easy to do.

“It is not a great feeling giving them up. It is definitely hard, it’s heartbreaking. You put your time, energy, effort, soul, love, into these dogs for a year to 16 months of your life. You become attached to them.”

But Meghan says knowing that the puppy is going on to do great things is such a reward.

“Seeing how much they help and seeing them graduate as a guide dog is absolutely incredible.”

Incredible to see them become a best friend, and give someone life-changing independence - someone like her father. Southeastern Guide Dogs says they’re always looking for puppy raiser volunteers - a job that Meghan says it’s so worth it.

그녀의 열정은 앞을 못 보는 아빠가 마네티 카운티에 있는 사우스이스턴 안내견 센터에서 첫 안내견을 받았을 때부터 시작되었는데, 그녀는 안내견이 아빠에게 얼마나 도움이 되었는 지를 눈으로 확인했습니다. “아빠가 안내견을 활용할 때는 원하는 것을 뭐든지 할 수 있었습니다. 아빠 혼자 산책을 다닐 수도 있었습니다. 슈퍼마켓에도 갈 수 있었습니다.”
그런 열정으로 메간은 꿈을 이루게 되었습니다. 이제 그녀는 사우스이스턴 안내견 센터에서 다섯 번째 안내견 강아지를 훈련시키고 있습니다. 그녀는 강아지들을 1년 정도 키우면서 돌려보내기 전까지 안내견으로서의 기본을 가르치는데, 그것이 쉽지는 않다고 말합니다.
“강아지들을 돌려줘야 할 때는 마음이 좋지 않습니다. 아주 힘들고 마음 아픈 일입니다. 자신의 인생에서 1년에서 16개월 정도의 시간을 들여 에너지, 노력, 마음, 사랑을 쏟아붓고 애착을 느끼기 때문입니다.” 하지만 그 강아지가 멋진 일들을 수행해 낼 것이라는 사실이 큰 보람이라고 메간은 말합니다.

title: Cincinnati Fans Travel for Playoff Game
koreanTitle: 플레이오프 경기를 보기 위해 먼 길을 나선 신시내티 주립대학 미식축구 팬들
rawContent:
Excitement. “I’m going to the bowl game!”

Anticipation. “We have high hopes.”

Whether a long-time fan... “I’ve been a season ticket holder since the late 80’s.”

Or a newcomer... “... my first college football game.”

Fans at CVG traveling to Dallas for the Cotton Bowl Friday have at least one thing in common: love for their ‘Cats.’

“I’m a huge UC fan. My wife graduated from there. I’m married into the UC family and I cannot be more excited for the team and the community.”

Congressman Brad Wenstrup says it’s been a thrilling season.

“We knew every game had to be won. So you just stayed on the edge of your seat all season long.”

Kevin Tatum says he and his wife knew they’d be packing their bags once the game was announced.

“I was immediately searching for tickets, searching for flights. And I cannot wait. I’m so excited.”

UC students Ryan Sawyer and Claudia Wright say they’re ecstatic Cincinnati’s being put on a pedestal.

“No one thinks of like Ohio whenever they think of football. So I think this is gonna be (cool)... especially with Ohio State and stuff. It’s awesome that Cincinnati is getting some recognition.”

As for game predictions?

“UC by four.” - “UC’s gonna win. I think so.” - “UC’s gonna win. What kind of question is that, come on!”

And, of course, the politically correct prediction.

“We got a great team with a lot of talent. And obviously Alabama does too. So I don’t want to make any predictions.”

title: New Year, Continued Omicron Surge
koreanTitle: 오미크론 변이종이 계속 급증하는 가운데 맞는 새해
rawContent:
New year continues to surge as Americans prepare to ring in 2022. The US new COVID case average sets a fourth record in four days fueled by omicron.

“Every day it’s a struggle to find beds to put patients in.”

Hospitals in hot spots feeling the heat. This week, compared to last, 18 states seeing at least 10 percent more hospitalizations. In Louisiana, Washington DC, Florida and Hawaii, hospitalizations have risen at least 50 percent in that time.

“Currently, we’re not as bad as we have been at, at kind of the peak times of COVID, but I think we are... definitely have the ability to get there by how many positive cases we’re seeing.”

Pediatric hospital admissions reached a record high. Most of those patients, unvaccinated. A concern, as only about 14 percent of kids ages 5 to 11 are fully vaccinated compared to 53 percent of those between 12 and 17 years old.

“And I’m really worried that we’re gonna be in for a tidal wave of admissions particularly for kids in the coming weeks.”

Meanwhile, Pfizer is expected to soon get authorization for booster shots for millions of children ages 12 to 15 according to a source familiar with the plan.

“Just being in the hospital is, is absolutely just terrifying, so it’s so important to try to minimize that risk by protecting them.”

It lets you press a button and the exterior quickly changes colors thanks to a body wrap on the vehicle. BMW says you could also have the vehicle flash different colors if you’re trying to find it in a crowded parking lot. No word on when the feature will be available on a BMW vehicle.

title: CES 2022
rawContent:
“The show must go on.” That’s the approach by CES, the global, annual tech showcase hosted by the Consumer Technology Association.

“Bringing people together this week hopefully lets us solve future problems, and again getting us living, working, playing better, all thanks to technology.”

After an all-virtual show last year, CES was supposed to return to full form on the Las Vegas Strip this week but Omicron had other plans. Big names such as Amazon, Meta, and Google are participating virtually. So is General Motors which took the reveal of its Chevrolet Silverado electric vehicle online.

On the floor which requires being vaccinated and masked are names like Samsung showing off a more affordable addition to its Galaxy S21 family of smartphones, with the Galaxy S21 FE, and the Freestyle, a tiny home projector for movies, TV and more.

Beyond big names, CES Spokesperson Allison Fried says in-person connections at the show are vital to small companies.

“This is their time to shine. These are people who have brilliant, innovative ideas that are trying to get it to market. And that market is at CES.”

That includes more in the fitness and health arena in the COVID-19 era.

“Telemedicine, digital therapeutics, remote patient monitoring systems, is a big deal right now as sensor technology is getting smaller and smaller.”

The show will wrap up on Friday, one day earlier than initially planned.

title: COVID: January Surge
rawContent:
Across the US, a 7-day average of more than 600,000 new COVID-19 cases a day. Hospitalizations nearing a record high.

“Omicron has rapidly become the predominant variant and cases have substantially increased to rates higher than we have seen at any point throughout this pandemic.”

COVID-19 cases in children reach a record level, too. With that, new CDC guidance to help slow the spread in K through 12 schools. The agency says unvaccinated children exposed to the virus should quarantine for at least five days after that exposure. Infected students, teachers and staff should isolate for at least five full days. After that masks are recommended around others for another five days. The agency also urges some extracurricular and sports activities to be canceled or go virtual to protect in-person learning.

“If we have the will to invest in public health and we work together, we can get to the point that COVID is something that we live with, we’re just not there yet.”

Some US health experts say co-existing with COVID may mean variant-specific vaccines.

“If we update our vaccines to match the Omicron variant not only can we re-establish both arms of powerful immunity, but we can also be better prepared for the next change of the virus.”

Experts say using the tools we have against COVID-19 like vaccines... will allow us to control this virus like we do the flu.

title: BOA, Auto Prices, Arby’s And Girl Scout Cookies

rawContent:

Consumer advocacy groups say the fees hit low-income Americans especially hard. Overdraft fees bring in billions for banks -- $15 billion in 2019, according to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau. Bank of America will also eliminate entirely its fee on bounced checks, or when there are insufficient funds in an account.

No relief in sight for buyers of new and used cars. It’s expected to be months before the auto market returns to normal, according to JD Power. Pent-up demand and low inventory continues to drive prices higher. The average transaction price for a new car is now $45,872 -- that’s higher than the suggested retail price. And almost 90% of shoppers are now paying more than the sticker price, or within 5% of it.

Arby’s new sandwich is so spicy it comes with a free vanilla shake to help cool you down. Called the Diablo Dare it comes in two versions -- crispy chicken and smoked brisket. Arby’s uses ghost pepper jack cheese, hot seasoning, jalapenos and a special barbecue sauce to give the sandwich its heat. An executive at the chain says the Diablo Dare is quote -- “not for the faint of heart.” You can get the sandwich and the shake for $5.99 now through February th at Arby’s nationwide.

Girl scouts teaming up with Door Dash to get Girl Scout Cookies to you. Door Dash will be the exclusive on-demand delivery company for the treats. You’ll be able to have thin mints, Somoas, and a new cookie called “Adventurfuls” delivery. Girl Scout Cookies can be ordered this month for pick up or delivery through the Door Dash app and website.

rawContent:

The community came together to mark the occasion with a birthday parade. Her first stop was the church she was baptized in as a child and where she later got married.

“I’ll have one taco ground beef.” - “One taco ground beef.” - “The dollar two.” - “For a dollar two, yeah.”

And Alma Bakery & Sweet Shop...

Friends say it’s the perfect example of Evelyn’s impact.

“She always has a smile on her face. She’s never says an unkind word about anyone. She’s just a very kind, loving, beautiful person inside and out.”

And, Evelyn says it’s hard to put into words just how much this means to her.

“I don’t know how to explain it, it’s just exciting. It’s exciting. I can’t believe it... do this for me.”

title: Australian Court Denies Djokovic Visa Appeal

rawContent:

Does that mean that Novak Djokovic makes Belgrade his first stop from Melbourne? We simply don’t know at this point.

Vučić also did not mince words in his feelings toward what Australia has done here. He called this harassment of unprecedented proportions, media lynching and said that it’s not Novak who should be humiliated... it is the Australian authorities who have humiliated themselves with what they have done.

Serbian state broadcaster, the public broadcaster this morning as this news was breaking, had it in their headline, simply one word, which was “disgrace.”

People here, by and large will tell you that this is political. This is all a move to try to win public support for a unpopular policy in Australia, perhaps ahead of an election. The Prime Minister’s office here says that, look, Novak Djokovic, “if you were to get vaccinated, it would do wonders for the lagging vaccination rates in this country.” But if you ask most people, they’ll tell you, look, this is up to each individual person, this is a personal choice. And the Australians are, are debating or had been debating whether or not Djokovic’s presence there would sort of stir up anti-vax sentiment. But I have to tell you this is not how Novak Djokovic is seen in this country as a sort of anti-vaxxer. Not by any stretch of the imagination.
